catalog_quote: Gizey is an unwritten tonal language. [...] For a full description of the tonal system of Gizey, refer to De Dominicis (2007). [p. 74:] 4. The Tones. Gizey is a tonal language. Experimental findings (De Dominicis 2007) demonstrate the linguistic function of two tonal registers (H and L). Particularly, the H/L tones oppose some minimal pairs both lexically and grammatically. [p. 75:] In the former case, a list of nouns opposed according to tone has been identified; in the latter case, the tonal opposition expresses the verbal aspect (accomplished/unaccomplished). This tonal function occurs in many languages belonging to central Chadic branch, such as for instance, Masa. Nevertheless, field research (De Dominicis 2007) has allowed us to verify the weak functional load had by tonal oppositions in Gizey[20]. new_statements.quote: Gizey is an unwritten tonal language. [p. 74:] Gizey is a tonal language. Experimental findings (De Dominicis 2007) demonstrate the linguistic function of two tonal registers (H and L). Particularly, the H/L tones oppose some minimal pairs both lexically and grammatically. [...] Nevertheless, field research (De Dominicis 2007) has allowed us to verify the weak functional load had by tonal oppositions in Gizey. As a consequence, it can be argued that linguistic tones in Gizey play a minor linguistic function and are probably destined to disappear, as their tonal system is endangered.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only full phonological description of Gizey treats it as a two-register (H/L) tone language with lexical and aspectual tonal contrasts of weak functional load; it contains no statement about word stress or accent at all (the words 'stress'/'accent' appear only in bibliography titles). No opened source locates a word stress in Gizey.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the sketch notes roots are maximally disyllabic (compounds, ideophones, toponyms, loans excepted) but says nothing about prominence.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology (roots, suffixed nouns, verbs) and tone; De Dominicis 2010 treats intonation-phrase prominences ('sentence stress') only as a general concept, not as a Gizey word-stress rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 gize1234 is a language-level languoid (NOCODE_Gizey) in the Masa section beside Masana [masa1322]; Glottolog also lists 'Gizay' [giza1238] as a dialect of Masana, and Ethnologue folds Gizey into Masana [mcn]. De Dominicis' data are from Djougoumta (Mayo-Danay, Guéré, Far North Cameroon; 10 speakers); Ajello 2005 and Guitang 2021 treat Gizey as a distinct language not mutually intelligible with Masa. The Masa-language check (masa1322) had already filed De Dominicis' Gizey tone papers under Masa; they belong here.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. p. 1: 'Gizey is an unwritten tonal language.' Sec. 4 'The Tones' pp. 74-75: two tonal registers H/L, lexical minimal pairs and verbal aspect marked by tone, weak functional load, tonal system 'endangered'. 'stress'/'accent' appear only in bibliography titles. Sections: vowels/consonants, syllable structure (roots max two syllables), vowel harmony, metaphony, final vowels, tones. downloaded from Internet Archive copy 2018-04-22 (journal host humnet.unipi.it dead).
